claims.text: DFT+U can reliably determine whether a ferromagnetic state is the ground state.
Optimized on-site U parameters for transition-metal d orbitals are generally in the range of 3–5 eV.
DFT+U accurately captures strong electron correlations relevant to competing magnetic configurations.
Strong electron correlations distinguish subtle total-energy differences between magnetic configurations.
The target is a transition-metal compound with multiple competing magnetic orderings at 0 K.
The proposed calculation uses DFT+U with U values around 3–5 eV and a dense k-point grid.
At 0 K, quantum-mechanical exchange interactions are dominant in the proposed system.
Electron correlations are significant in the proposed system.
On-site Coulomb interactions affect electron localization and the local electronic structure of transition-metal d orbitals.
Adding an optimized Hubbard U improves the treatment of strong electron correlations.
Improved treatment of correlations permits more precise total-energy calculations for competing magnetic states.
Total-energy differences between competing magnetic configurations determine which configuration is the ground state.
If ferromagnetism is the ground state, DFT+U will assign the ferromagnetic configuration a lower total energy than the competing configurations.
Standard DFT without Hubbard U may fail to resolve subtle magnetic energy differences because it treats electron-correlation effects inadequately.
Static DFT+U may be insufficient when dynamic correlation effects are significant.
The reliability of DFT+U depends on determining an appropriate material-specific U parameter.
Calculated magnetic energy differences must be robust against variation of computational parameters.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome is conditional: DFT+U should rank the ferromagnetic state lowest only if it is actually the ground state. The falsification rule instead treats failure to rank ferromagnetism lowest as falsifying the method, even though that result could correctly indicate a non-ferromagnetic ground state.
